easy.explanation: Samuel said, “The Lord sent me to anoint thee to be king.”
easy.q: Who sent Samuel to anoint Saul king?

easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Saul to smite Amalek.
easy.q: Whom was Saul commanded to smite?

easy.explanation: Saul was told to “utterly destroy all that they have.”
easy.q: What was Saul commanded to do to all that Amalek had?

answers: To remind him of his commission and responsibility
To ask him to build a city
medium.explanation: Saul’s royal position was connected to his responsibility to obey the Lord.
medium.q: Why did Samuel remind Saul that he had been anointed king?

answers: Amalek laid wait for Israel on the way from Egypt
medium.explanation: The Lord remembered what Amalek did to Israel when Israel came up from Egypt.
medium.q: What reason did the Lord give for the command against Amalek?

answers: Destroy completely according to the command
medium.explanation: The command required complete destruction and instructed Saul not to spare them.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “utterly destroy” mean?

answers: A king may act only according to his own will
A king is responsible to carry out God’s commission
A king must listen only to the people
challenge.explanation: Saul was king under the Lord’s authority and was required to obey the Lord’s word.
challenge.q: What leadership principle appears in Samuel’s words to Saul?

challenge.explanation: The detailed list emphasizes that the command applied broadly to people and possessions.
challenge.q: What does the list “man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass” emphasize?

answers: Hearing and obeying the Lord was necessary for fulfilling the mission
It was unnecessary for a king
It was required only of the people
challenge.explanation: Samuel begins by commanding Saul to hearken to the Lord’s words before giving the mission.
challenge.q: What is the connection between hearkening to the Lord’s voice and Saul’s mission?

paragraphs.title: The Campaign and the Sparing of Agag and the Spoil

easy.explanation: Saul gathered two hundred thousand footmen.
easy.q: How many footmen did Saul gather, according to the passage?

easy.explanation: Saul told the Kenites to depart from among the Amalekites.
easy.q: Whom did Saul warn to depart from among the Amalekites?

easy.explanation: Saul took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive.

answers: They had shown kindness to Israel
They were the king of Amalek
medium.explanation: Saul remembered that the Kenites had shown kindness to Israel when Israel came out of Egypt.
medium.q: Why did Saul warn the Kenites?

answers: Agag was kept alive, while the people were destroyed
Agag escaped, while the people remained
medium.explanation: Saul took Agag alive but utterly destroyed the people with the sword.
medium.q: What was the difference between Agag’s fate and the people’s fate?

answers: He spared Agag and the best sheep and oxen
medium.explanation: Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the spoil.
medium.q: Which action shows that Saul did not fully obey the command?

answers: The command made no distinction between Amalek and others
There was a distinction between Amalek and those who did not belong to it
challenge.explanation: The Kenites were told to separate from the Amalekites so they would not be destroyed with them.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from saving the Kenites before the battle?

answers: The finest part of the spoil
challenge.explanation: “Best” refers to the finest and most valuable animals.
challenge.q: What does “the best of the sheep, and of the oxen” mean in context?

answers: Saul acted contrary to the explicit command
The command concerned only the Kenites
challenge.explanation: The Lord commanded Saul not to spare, but Saul and the people spared Agag and the best animals.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between “spare them not” and “spared Agag” show?

easy.explanation: The word of the Lord came unto Samuel.
easy.q: To whom did the word of the Lord come concerning Saul?

answers: The bleating of sheep and lowing of oxen
easy.explanation: Samuel heard the bleating of the sheep and the lowing of the oxen.
easy.q: What did Samuel hear when he met Saul?

easy.explanation: Saul said that he had brought Agag the king of Amalek.
easy.q: What did Saul say he had done with Agag?

answers: Saul had turned back from following the Lord and had not performed His commandments
Saul had not gathered an army
medium.explanation: The Lord said Saul had turned back from following Him and had not performed His commandments.
medium.q: Why did the Lord repent that He had made Saul king?

answers: The people spared it to sacrifice unto the Lord
The spoil belonged to the Kenites
Samuel commanded them to bring it
medium.explanation: Saul claimed that the people spared the best animals to sacrifice unto the Lord.
medium.q: How did Saul explain the presence of the spoil?

answers: I regret or am grieved over the decision
medium.explanation: The phrase expresses the Lord’s grief over having made Saul king.
medium.q: What does “It repenteth me” mean in this passage?

answers: The spoil’s sounds immediately showed that everything had not been destroyed
challenge.explanation: The bleating sheep and lowing oxen contradicted Saul’s claim of complete obedience.
challenge.q: What creates the irony in Saul’s claim, “I have performed the commandment of the Lord”?

answers: Samuel tested Saul’s claim against the observable facts
Samuel did not care about the command
Samuel wanted the spoil for himself
challenge.explanation: Samuel confronted Saul with the evidence he could hear.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Samuel’s response to the animal sounds?

answers: His prayer preceded his confrontation with Saul after hearing of Saul’s rejection
challenge.explanation: After hearing the Lord’s judgment, Samuel cried unto the Lord all night and then went to meet Saul.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Samuel’s prayer all night and the morning meeting?

paragraphs.title: Royal Responsibility and the Primacy of Obedience

answers: He was the head of the tribes of Israel and king
easy.explanation: Samuel reminded Saul that he had been made head of the tribes of Israel and anointed king.
easy.q: What did Samuel remind Saul about his position?

easy.explanation: Samuel asked why Saul had “flown upon the spoil.”
easy.q: What did Samuel say Saul had done with the spoil?

answers: To obey the voice of the Lord
easy.explanation: Samuel said, “To obey is better than sacrifice.”
easy.q: What did Samuel say was better than sacrifice?

answers: To perform the Lord’s word completely
Always to prefer the people’s wishes
medium.explanation: The Lord had sent Saul to destroy Amalek, so Saul was responsible to obey fully.
medium.q: What was Saul’s responsibility as a leader?

answers: Obedience to the Lord comes before sacrifice
medium.explanation: Samuel taught that obeying the Lord is better than offering sacrifices.
medium.q: Why could sacrifice not justify taking the spoil?

medium.explanation: Samuel said, “For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft.”
medium.q: What did Samuel compare to the sin of witchcraft?

answers: The fact that the people fought
challenge.explanation: Samuel’s central accusation is that Saul rejected the Lord’s word and failed to obey.
challenge.q: What does Samuel identify as the root problem: the sacrifice or the disobedience?

answers: Listening and obeying are more important than a rich sacrifice
The fat of rams should be eaten
Sacrifice is more important than obedience
challenge.explanation: Samuel contrasts obedience with the valuable fat offered in sacrifice.
challenge.q: What does “to hearken than the fat of rams” mean?

answers: From recalling Saul’s position to exposing his disobedience and announcing his rejection
From praising Saul to making Agag king
From warning the Kenites to gathering the army
challenge.explanation: Samuel recalls Saul’s authority, challenges his disobedience, and declares that the Lord has rejected him as king.
challenge.q: How does Samuel’s argument develop in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Saul’s Admission and the Symbolic Tearing

easy.explanation: Saul confessed, “I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.”
easy.q: Whom did Saul say he feared?

easy.explanation: When Samuel turned away, he laid hold of the skirt of his mantle, and it rent.
easy.q: What happened to the skirt of Samuel’s mantle?

answers: Return with him so that he might worship the Lord
easy.explanation: Saul asked Samuel to turn again with him so that he might worship the Lord.
easy.q: What did Saul ask Samuel to do?

answers: Transgressed the commandment of the Lord and Samuel’s words
medium.explanation: Saul admitted, “I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words.”
medium.q: What did Saul confess that he had done?

answers: The kingdom of Israel being rent from Saul
medium.explanation: Samuel said, “The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day.”
medium.q: What did the torn mantle symbolize?

answers: He did not want to be publicly disgraced
He wanted to receive the spoil
He wanted to appoint a new king
medium.explanation: Saul asked Samuel to honor him before the elders and Israel.
medium.q: Why did Saul ask to be honored before the elders and Israel?

answers: He admits his sin while still caring about his public standing
challenge.explanation: Saul confesses his sin but also asks to be honored before the people.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Saul’s confession and his request for honor?

answers: The Lord’s decision is not an ordinary human change of mind
challenge.explanation: Samuel emphasizes that the Lord is not like a man who lies or changes his decision.
challenge.q: What does “the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent” teach?

answers: He returned with Saul so Saul would not be publicly disgraced
challenge.explanation: Samuel would not return in fellowship as Saul requested, but he did turn again after Saul so Saul could worship.
challenge.q: What did Samuel do after refusing to reverse the judgment?

paragraphs.title: Agag’s Judgment and the End of the Relationship

easy.explanation: Samuel commanded that Agag be brought to him.

answers: Hewed him in pieces before the Lord
easy.explanation: Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.
easy.q: What did Samuel do to Agag?
Where did Samuel go at the end of the chapter?

answers: He thought the bitterness of death was past
medium.explanation: Agag said, “Surely the bitterness of death is past.”
medium.q: What did Agag think when he was brought before Samuel?

answers: Samuel saw Saul no more until the day of his death
medium.explanation: The passage says Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death.
medium.q: What happened to the relationship between Samuel and Saul?

medium.explanation: Samuel mourned for Saul, although the Lord repented that He had made Saul king.
medium.q: What did Samuel do concerning Saul at the end?

answers: It completes the command not to leave Agag alive
It proves that the Kenites were the enemy
challenge.explanation: Agag had been spared contrary to the command, so Samuel carried out his judgment at the end.
challenge.q: How is Agag’s judgment connected to the command at the beginning of the chapter?

answers: Samuel departs and mourns, while Saul returns to his house
They both go together to Ramah
Saul mourns and Samuel becomes king
challenge.explanation: Samuel went to Ramah and mourned, while Saul went up to his house at Gibeah.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Samuel and Saul at the end?

answers: The Lord regretted making Saul king, and Samuel’s relationship with him ended
Saul received unconditional approval to reign
challenge.explanation: The final verse records the Lord’s regret and Samuel’s separation from Saul.
challenge.q: What does the ending indicate about Saul’s kingship?
